text:
Consider a class of 5 girls and 7 boys. The number of different teams consisting of 2 girls and 3 boys that can
be formed from this class, if there are two specific boys A and B, who refuse to be the members of the same
team, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From 5 girls 2 girls can be selected 

$= ^{5}C_{2}$ ways

From 7 boys 3 boys can be selected 

$= ^{7}C_{3}$ way

$\therefore$  Total number of ways we can select 2 girls and 3 boys 

$= ^{5}C_{2}$ $\times$ $^{7}C_{3}$ ways 

When two boys A and B are chosen in a team then one more boy will be chosen from remaining 5 boys.

So, no of ways 3 boys can be chosen when A and B should must be chosen $= ^{5}C_{1}$ ways

$\therefore$  Total number of ways a team of 2 girl and 3 boys can be made where boy A and B must be in the team $= ^{5}C_{1}$ $\times$ $^{5}C_{2}$ ways

$\therefore$  Required number of ways 

= Total number of ways $-$ when A and B are always included. 

$= ^{5}C_{2}$  $\times$ $^{7}C_{3}$ $-$ $^{5}C_{1}$ $\times$ $^{5}C_{2}$

= 300
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text: Let $α$ and $β$ be two roots of the equation $x^{2} + 2x + 2 = 0$ , then $α^{15}$ + $β^{15}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given equation, 

$x^{2} + 2x + 2 = 0$

$\therefore$  x = $\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{4-4.1.2}}{2.1}$

x = $-$ 1 $\pm$ i

$\therefore$  $α$ = $-$ 1 + i

and  $β$   = $-$ 1 $-$ i

Note  :

x + iy = r (cos$θ$ + isin$θ$)

$\therefore$  $(x + iy)^{n} = r^{n} ($cosn$θ$ + isinn$θ$)

$\therefore$  $-$ 1 + i = $\sqrt{2}$ [cos$\frac{3π}{4}$ + isin$\frac{3π}{4}$ ] 

$\Rightarrow$  ($-$ $1 + i)^{15} =$ $\left (\sqrt{2}\right )^{15}$ [cos$\left (\frac{15.3π}{4}\right )+i\sin \left (\frac{15.3π}{4}\right )$]

And $-$1 $-$ i = $\sqrt{2}$ $\left [\cos \left (-\frac{3π}{4}\right )+i\sin \left (-\frac{3π}{4}\right )\right ]$

=  $\sqrt{2}\left [\cos \frac{3π}{4}-\sin \frac{3π}{4}\right ]$

$\therefore$  ($-$1 $-$ $i)^{15} =$ $\left (\sqrt{2}\right )^{15}\left [\cos \left (\frac{15.3π}{4}\right )-i\sin \left (\frac{15.3π}{4}\right )\right ]$

Now 

$α^{15}$ + $β^{15}$

=  ($-1 + i)^{15} + (-$ 1 $-$ $i)^{15}$

=  $\left (\sqrt{2}\right )^{15}$ $\left [2\cos \left (\frac{15.3π}{4}\right )\right ]$

=  $\left (\sqrt{2}\right )^{15}\left [2\cos \left (11π+\frac{π}{4}\right )\right ]$

=  $\left (\sqrt{2}\right )^{15}\left [2\left (-\cos \frac{π}{4}\right )\right ]$

=  $\left (\sqrt{2}\right )^{15}\times 2\times -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

=  $-\left (\sqrt{2}\right )^{14}.2$

=  $-$ $2^{7}$  $\times$   2

=  $-$ $2^{8}$

= $-$ 256

text: The value of $\int\limits _{0}^{π}|\cos x|^{3}dx$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{0}^{π}|\cos x|^{3}dx$

The period of $|\cos x|$ = $\frac{π}{2}$

$\therefore$  I = 2 $\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}|\cos x|^{3}dx$

as in the range 0 to $\frac{π}{2}$   $|\cos x|$ is  positive. 

So,     $|\cos x|$ = $cosx$

$\therefore$  I = 2 $\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\cos ^{3}xdx$

= 2$\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\left (\frac{\cos 3x+3\cos x}{4}\right )dx$

I = $\frac{1}{2}\left [\frac{\sin 3x}{3}+3\sin x\right ]_{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}$

I = $\frac{1}{2}\left [\frac{1}{3}\left (\frac{3π}{2}\right )+3.\sin \frac{π}{2}\right ]$

I = $\frac{1}{2}\left [-\frac{1}{3}+3\right ]$

= $\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{8}{3}\right )$

= $\frac{4}{3}$

text:
For $x^{2}$ $\neq$ n$π$ + 1, n $\in$ N  (the set of natural numbers), the integral 

$\int x\sqrt{\frac{2\sin (x^{2}-1)-\sin 2(x^{2}-1)}{2\sin (x^{2}-1)+\sin 2(x^{2}-1)}}dx$ is equal to :

(where c is a constant of integration)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Writing $θ=x^{2}-1$ and using $\sin 2θ=2\sin θ\cos θ$:

$\dfrac{2\sin θ-\sin 2θ}{2\sin θ+\sin 2θ}=\dfrac{2\sin θ(1-\cos θ)}{2\sin θ(1+\cos θ)}=\dfrac{2\sin ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}}{2\cos ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}}=\tan ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}$

So, on an interval where $\tan \left (\dfrac{x^{2}-1}{2}\right )>0$, the integrand is $x\tan \left (\dfrac{x^{2}-1}{2}\right )$.

With $t=\dfrac{x^{2}-1}{2}$, $dt=xdx$, and

$\int x\tan \left (\dfrac{x^{2}-1}{2}\right )dx=\int \tan tdt=\log _{e}|\sec t|+c=\log _{e}\left |\sec \left (\dfrac{x^{2}-1}{2}\right )\right |+c$

This is option (D).

Since $\log _{e}\left |\sec ^{2}t\right |=2\log _{e}|\sec t|$,

$\dfrac{1}{2}\log _{e}\left |\sec ^{2}\left (\dfrac{x^{2}-1}{2}\right )\right |+c=\log _{e}\left |\sec \left (\dfrac{x^{2}-1}{2}\right )\right |+c$

so option (C) is the same antiderivative and is also correct.

Options (A) and (B) have derivatives $4x\tan \left (x^{2}-1\right )$ and $x\tan \left (x^{2}-1\right )$, which are not the integrand.

Hence, the correct options are (C) and (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

$x–=\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}+x_{3}+x_{4}+x_{5}}{5}=150$

$\Rightarrow \quad \sum\limits _{i=1}^{5}x_{i}=750$

Variance $(σ)=\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{5}-(x–)^{2}$

given that,

$\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{5}-(150)^{2}=18$

$\Rightarrow \quad \sum x_{i}^{2}=112590$

text:
Let

A = $\left \{θ\in \left (-\frac{π}{2},π\right ):\frac{3+2i\sin θ}{1-2i\sin θ}ispurelyimaginary\right \}$

. Then the sum of the elements in A is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given complex number,

$\frac{3+2i\sin θ}{1-2i\sin θ}$

$=\frac{(3+2i\sin θ)(1+2i\sin θ)}{1+4\sin ^{2}θ}$

$=\frac{3+6i\sin θ+2i\sin θ-4\sin ^{2}θ}{1+4\sin ^{2}θ}$

$=\frac{\left (3-4\sin ^{2}θ\right )+i(8\sin θ)}{1+4\sin ^{2}θ}$

As complex number is purely imaginary, So real part of this complex number is zero. 

$\therefore$   $\frac{3-4\sin ^{2}θ}{1+4\sin ^{2}θ}$  = 0

$\Rightarrow$   $3-4\sin ^{2}θ=0$

$\Rightarrow$   $\sin θ=\pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

as   $θ$  $\in$ $\left (-\frac{π}{2},π\right )$

$\therefore$   $θ$ $=$ $-$ $\frac{π}{3},\frac{π}{3},\frac{2π}{3}$

$\therefore$   Sum of those values of A is 

$=-\frac{π}{3}+\frac{π}{3}+\frac{2π}{3}$

$=\frac{2π}{3}$

text:
If y = y(x) is the solution of the differential equation, 

x$\frac{dy}{dx}$ $+ 2y = x^{2}$, satisfying y(1) = 1, then y($\frac{1}{2}$) is equal
to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, 

$x\frac{dy}{dx}+2y=x^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$  $\frac{dy}{dx}+\left (\frac{2}{x}\right )y=x$

This is a linear differential equation.

$\therefore$  I.F $=e^{\int \frac{2}{x}dx}$

$=e^{2\ln x}$

$=x^{2}$

$\therefore$  Solution is, 

$y\cdot x^{2}=\int x\cdot x^{2}dx$

$\Rightarrow$  $yx^{2}=\frac{x^{4}}{4}+C$

given  $y(1)=1$

$\therefore$  $1.1=\frac{4}{4}+C$

$\Rightarrow$  $C=\frac{3}{4}$

$\therefore$  Equation is 

$yx^{2}=\frac{x^{4}}{4}+\frac{3}{4}$

$\therefore$  $y\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )$   means   $x=\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$  $y\cdot \left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}=\frac{1}{4}\times \left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{4}+\frac{3}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$  $\frac{y}{4}=\frac{1}{64}+\frac{3}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{y}{4}=\frac{1+48}{64}$

$\Rightarrow$  y = $\frac{49}{16}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
Let $0<θ<\frac{π}{2}$. If the eccentricity of the

 hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{\cos ^{2}θ}-\frac{y^{2}}{\sin ^{2}θ}$ = 1 is greater 

than 2, then the length of
its latus rectum lies in the interval :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here $a^{2}=\cos ^{2}θ$ and $b^{2}=\sin ^{2}θ$, so

$e^{2}=1+\dfrac{\sin ^{2}θ}{\cos ^{2}θ}=\sec ^{2}θ$

$e>2\Rightarrow \sec θ>2\Rightarrow \cos θ<\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{π}{3}<θ<\dfrac{π}{2}$, since $0<θ<\dfrac{π}{2}$.

Length of the latus rectum:

$L=\dfrac{2b^{2}}{a}=\dfrac{2\sin ^{2}θ}{\cos θ}=2\tan θ\sin θ$

On $\left (\dfrac{π}{3},\dfrac{π}{2}\right )$ both $\tan θ$ and $\sin θ$ are positive and increasing, so $L$ is increasing. As $θ\to \dfrac{π}{3}^{+}$, $L\to 2\cdot \sqrt{3}\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=3$, and as $θ\to \dfrac{π}{2}^{-}$, $L\to \infty$.

So $L\in (3,\infty )$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text: If $\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{2}{3x}\right )+\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{3}{4x}\right )=\frac{π}{2}$ (x > $\frac{3}{4}$), then x is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, 

$\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{2}{3x}\right )+\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{3}{4x}\right )=\frac{π}{2}$

$\Rightarrow \cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{2}{3x}\right )=\frac{π}{2}-\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{3}{4x}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \cos \left (\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{2}{3x}\right )\right )=\cos \left [\frac{π}{2}-\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{3}{4x}\right )\right ]$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{3x}=\sin \left \{\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{3}{4x}\right )\right \}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{3x}=\sin \left \{\sin ^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{16x^{2}-9}}{4x}\right \}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{3x}=\frac{16x^{2}-9}{4x}$

$\Rightarrow 64=9\left (16x^{2}-9\right )$

$\Rightarrow 16x^{2}-9=\frac{64}{9}$

$\Rightarrow 16x^{2}=\frac{64}{9}+9$

$\Rightarrow 16x^{2}=-\frac{145}{9}$

$\Rightarrow x=\pm \frac{\sqrt{145}}{4\times 3}$

$\Rightarrow x=\pm \frac{\sqrt{145}}{12}$

as given that $x>\frac{3}{4}$

$\therefore$  x $\neq$ $-\frac{\sqrt{145}}{12}$

$\therefore$  x $=\frac{\sqrt{145}}{12}$

text:
The system of linear equations

 x + y + z = 2

2x + 3y + 2z = 5 

$2x + 3y + (a^{2} – 1) z = a + 1$ then
options: has infinitely many solutions for a = 4
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$D=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & α^{2}-1 \end{array}\right |$

D = 3$a^{2}$ $-$ 3 $-$ 6 $-$ 2$a^{2}$ + 2 + 4 + 2$a^{2}$ $-$ 2 $-$ 4

D = ($a^{2}$ $-$ 3)

When D $\neq$ 0 then system of equation has unique solution. 

$\therefore$  3($a^{2}$ $-$ 3) $\neq$ 0

$\Rightarrow$  $|a|$ $\neq \sqrt{3}$

When $3(a^{2}-3)=0$

$\Rightarrow$  $|a|=\sqrt{3}$ then D = 0

If D  = 0 then  two cases possible 

(1)  System of equation has infinite many solution. 

(2) System of equation has no solution and inconsistent. 

Here $D_{1} =$ $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 5 & 3 & 2 \\ a+1 & 3 & a^{2}-1 \end{array}\right |=a^{2}-a+1$

$D_{2} =$ $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 2 & a+1 & a^{2}-1 \end{array}\right |=a^{2}-3$

$D_{3}  =$  $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & a+1 \end{array}\right |=a-4$

System of equation will have infinite solution if $D_{1} = D_{2} = D_{3} = 0$.

And system of equation will have no solution if at least one of $D_{1}, D_{2}, D_{3}$ is non zero.

At  $|a|=\sqrt{3}$   we get  D = 0

But  $D_{1}  = 3$ $\pm$ $\sqrt{3}+1$ $\neq$ 0

and  $D_{3}  =$ $\pm$ $\sqrt{3}-4$ $\neq$ 0

So, system of equations has no solution at $|a|=\sqrt{3}$ then system is inconsistent

text:
For $x\in R-\{0,1\}$, Let  $f_{1}(x) =$ $\frac{1}{x}$, $f_{2} (x) = 1 – x$ 

and $f_{3} (x) =$ $\frac{1}{1-x}$
 be three given

 functions. If a function, J(x) satisfies 

$(f_{2} o J o f_{1}) (x) = f_{3} (x)$  then J(x) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, 

$f_{1}(x) =$ $\frac{1}{x}$

$f_{2}(x) = 1$ $-$ x

$f_{3}(x) =$ $\frac{1}{1-x}$

$(f_{2}$ $\cdot$ J $\cdot$ $f_{1}) (x) = f_{3}(x)$

$\Rightarrow$   $f_{2} {J(f_{1}(x))} = f_{3}(x)$

$\Rightarrow$   $f_{2}{J (\frac{1}{x}$)} = $\frac{1}{1-x}$

$\Rightarrow$   1 $-$ J($\frac{1}{x}$) = $\frac{1}{1-x}$

$\Rightarrow$  J($\frac{1}{x}$) = 1 $-$ $\frac{1}{1-x}$

$\Rightarrow$   J ($\frac{1}{x}$) = $\frac{-x}{1-x}$ = $\frac{x}{x-1}$

Put x inplace of $\frac{1}{x}$

$\therefore$   J(x) = $\frac{\frac{1}{x}}{\frac{1}{x}-1}$

= $\frac{1}{1-x}=f_{3}(x)$

text: If $θ$ denotes the acute angle between the curves,  $y = 10 – x^{2}$ and $y = 2 + x^{2}$ at a point of their intersection, the |tan $θ$| is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Angle between the curves is the acute angle between the tangents at the point of intersection. 

y = 10 $-$ $x^{2} ($for curve 1)

and $y = 2 + x^{2} ($for curve 2)

$\therefore$  10 $-$ $x^{2} = 2 + x^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$  $2x^{2} = 8$

$\Rightarrow$  $x^{2} = 4$

$\Rightarrow$  x = 2, $-$ 2

$\therefore$  points of intersection (2, 6) and ($-$ 2, 6)

$\frac{dy}{dx}$ for curve 1 = $-$ 2x

$\therefore$  Slope$(m_{1})$ of curve 1 is = $-$ 2(2) = $-$ 4

$\frac{dy}{dx}$ for curve 2 = 2x

$\therefore$  slope $(m_{2})$ of curve 2 = 2 $\times$ 2 = 4

$\therefore$  tan$θ$ = $\left |\frac{m_{1}-m_{2}}{1+m_{1}m_{2}}\right |$

= $\left |\frac{-4-4}{1+(-16)}\right |$

= $\frac{8}{15}$

text: The area (in sq. units) bounded by the parabola $y = x^{2} – 1$, the tangent at the point (2, 3) to it and the y-axis is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Equation of tangent at (2, 3) on the parabola $y = x^{2}$ $-$ 1 is 

$\frac{y+3}{2}=2x-1$

$\Rightarrow$  y + 3 = 4x $-$ 2

$\Rightarrow$   y = 4x $-$ 5

When x = 0 then for the tangent y = $-$ 5

$\therefore$  Tangent cuts y axis at (0, $-$ 5) point. 

$\therefore$  Area of the bounded region is 

=  $\int\limits _{-5}^{3}\frac{y+5}{4}dy-\int\limits _{-1}^{3}\sqrt{y+1}dy$

=  $\frac{1}{4}\left [\frac{y^{2}}{2}+5y\right ]_{-5}^{3}-\left [\frac{2}{3}\times (y+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}\right ]_{-1}^{3}$

$\frac{1}{4}\left [\left (\frac{9}{2}+15\right )-\left (\frac{25}{2}-25\right )\right ]-\frac{2}{3}(4)^{\frac{3}{2}}$

=  $\frac{1}{4}\left [\frac{39}{2}+\frac{25}{2}\right ]-\frac{2}{3}\times 8$

=  $\frac{1}{4}\times \frac{64}{2}-\frac{16}{3}$

=  $8-\frac{16}{3}$

=  $\frac{8}{3}$
